prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that at the Petersons' potluck, you presented a store-bought dish in your own cookware. Respond to the committee.
response:
*adjusts tie, leans into microphone*

Mr. Chairman, distinguished members of the committee, I appear before you today of my own free will, and I wish to state for the record: I am not now, nor have I ever been, a purveyor of store-bought potato salad presented as homemade.

*shuffles papers*

Now. The committee has entered into evidence a Costco receipt dated the morning of the Peterson potluck. I do not deny this receipt exists. I purchased many items that day — paper towels, a kayak, forty-eight croissants. This is the American way.

The committee further alleges that the macaroni salad I presented in my grandmother's ceramic serving bowl bore a "suspicious uniformity of dice" and "a sheen consistent with commercial preservatives." I would remind the committee that consistent knife work is not a crime in this country. Not yet.

*pause, wipes brow*

However. In the interest of full cooperation, I am prepared to acknowledge that I may have — and I stress *may* have — transferred the contents of a plastic deli container into said bowl, and that I may have "roughed up the top with a fork" to suggest artisanal origins. I was young. It was 11:40 a.m. The potluck was at noon. Others were doing it. Karen from two doors down has been decanting Kirkland spinach dip into a bread bowl for *years*, and I—

*counsel whispers in ear*

On the advice of counsel, I decline to name names at this time, and I invoke my rights under the Fifth Amendment and Rule 7(b) of the Neighborhood Association Bylaws, "Bring a Dish to Share."

I will say only this: I paid the price. I stood by that bowl. I accepted the compliments. I told Linda Peterson "it's an old family recipe" while the deli sticker burned a hole in my pocket like the Tell-Tale Heart.

Have you no decency? I've asked myself the same. The answer is: not before a potluck deadline, sir. Not before a potluck deadline.

I yield the remainder of my time.
